notes.title: Dev Update: Answering Your Questions, First Batch
notes.content:
[p]Greetings, Commanders.
[/p][p]Today we’re sharing the first batch of answers to your questions. 

More will arrive next week, so if you haven’t asked anything yet, you can still post your question in the comments under this announcement!
    [/p][table equalcells="1" colwidth=","][tr][td][p][b]Question[/b][/p][/td][td][p][b]Answer[/b][/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]How confident are devs about early access within this year?[/p][/td][td][p]We’ll be able to determine that throughout our next beta cycle. Experiences of the past two years taught us not to commit to a release window unless we’re 100% confident in meeting them. Right now we can’t say more than that our goal is to deliver an experience that’s fun, stable, and runs well when it finally lands in your hands.[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]Will the silksong Release in any way Change the starminer Release?[/p][/td][td][p]No, the Silksong release did not in any way or form affect the release or development of Starminer.[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]will there be any lore previews and/or a dedicated discord server section with info and discussion on the lore? (They're doing something similar for Falling Frontier lately, so I thought something similar could be nice for Starminer also)[/p][/td][td][p]That is an interesting and lucrative idea - we will put more thought into it. The lore of Starminer is definitely something we will continuously expand and build upon with the help of our narrative designer Aidan.[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]will there be a feature for saving ships' and stations' blueprints and export them to share them, maybe through Steam Workshop?)[/p][/td][td][p]Yes! We’re working on a feature that will let players share their station blueprints with others. Right now you can already save and recall your own blueprints through the build menu - the next step is adding the backend that makes it possible to share them with the community. This feature will be available in-game.[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]Are there any plans to add planetary mining? Like maybe rare exotic resources that can only be obtained by first making a ship that can enter an atmosphere?[/p][/td][td][p]We don’t have plans to include planetary mining at release, but it’s definitely something that fits naturally into Starminer. It’s an idea we’ve already talked about internally, and in one form or another, it’s very likely to make its way into the game in the future.[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]Will there be community references in the game, like decals?[/p][/td][td][p]Good idea, we will definitely include some community easter eggs at some point.[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]Any chance we can have like a “early backer pay extra” option that gets our names in game like for NPCs or Star names?
I’d totally pay up to $10-15 more if it meant an NPC/location/whatever with my game tag[/p][/td][td][p]That's up to our publisher.[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]gamemodes question: probably a story mode, but what about "endless" or similar?
or is it more like rimworld in that its always story mode and always endless?[/p][/td][td][p]Starminer will launch with three game modes: Campaign, Sandbox, and Survival.
In Campaign, players progress through a series of missions designed to introduce both the core mechanics and the game’s lore. While there’s structure, the missions aren’t strictly linear and you’ll still have plenty of freedom in how you approach them.
Sandbox offers a more customizable experience, letting you choose your starting ship, resources, location, and whether enemies are active or not.
Survival is all about endurance: you’ll face endless waves of enemies and fight to stay alive as long as possible. All three game modes will continue to be refined and expanded during Early Access, guided by feedback from the community.[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]Is it out yet? (Sorry. I had to do it.... i will show myself out) Jokes aside though, im curious on scales. Scale of the universe, 
scale of ships, scale of factions etc. What kind of scale is the devs aiming to be "scope" if you will.[/p][/td][td][p]Nah, it's not out, sorry to disappoint :). As for scale: Starminer spans three star systems - Sol, Lalande, and Alpha Centauri - with more than 25 distinct environments. The campaign features dozens of missions of varying length and difficulty (and we are still adding more). Ships can be built as large as you like, with the only real limit being your CPU. Our aim is to keep the scope manageable for our small team, while still making the universe feel vast and alive.[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]build limits?[/p][/td][td][p]As mentioned earlier, there are no build limits. You can grow as big as you like - the only limit is what your computer can handle.[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]Space Sim has been a tremendous market. What’s the identity/ core focus of this project compared to iconic like 
Elite Dangerous, Eve, X4, etc?[/p][/td][td][p]The core focus of Starminer is creativity, customisation and physics. We want players to have the freedom to approach challenges in their own way, whether that means customizing a station, designing a ship, or experimenting with different strategies. Unlike large space sims like X4 or Elite Dangerous, Starminer places a strong emphasis on creative building and heavy customization. Another key distinction is our physics simulation: things like mass, thrust, and structural integrity really matter, adding a layer of depth and realism that sets the game apart from these heavyweight titles.[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]Will there be a 12 hour space ship docking scene?[/p][/td][td][p]Our team is still pondering on whether or not to include that feature.[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]Will ship controls by more direct (space engineers, elite dangerous) or more abstract (nebulous fleet command)[/p][/td][td][p]Direct ship controls are one of Starminer's key features, giving you full inputs across all six degrees of freedom. At the same time, we are developing a point-and-click navigation aid to help with long-distance travel or tricky maneuvers, but it is meant as a support tool rather than the main way to play the game.[/p][/td][/tr][tr][td][p]will there be power managment systems[/p][/td][td][p]You can manage your ship's power by toggling various systems on or off. Mining lasers, weapons, shields, refineries, and factories each have dedicated controls to switch them all at once, and you can also toggle individual modules if you want more fine-grained control over energy use.[/p][/td][/tr][/table]

This feature will be available in-game.

At the same time, we are developing a point-and-click navigation aid to help with long-distance travel or tricky maneuvers, but it is meant as a support tool rather than the main way to play the game.

notes.title: Weekly Screenshots #6 🌌
notes.content:
[h1]Starminer Weekly Screenshots #6 [/h1]

[h3]Welcome back, Commanders—let’s merge, build, and conquer the galaxy.[/h3] 

Today in [i][b]Starminer[/b][/i], we'll explore the art of building and merging your fleet. Whether it’s stacking station hubs to create massive structures or merging stations for a more unified operation or relaying energy from a solar rig, each decision plays a crucial role in optimizing your fleet and ensuring the success of your resource management in space.

[b][h2] Building Stronger Fleets through Station Merging 🛰️ [/h2][/b]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35809242/9fd39c371eb9b7511fbc5048907a9f4bc8385457.png[/img]
In [i][b]Starminer[/b][/i], it’s not all about warfare—sometimes, you'll find success comes from efficient resource management. Here we have a solar rig relaying excess energy to a small mining ship, ensuring that the fleet operates at full capacity. By optimizing energy distribution, this system supports the ongoing collection of valuable resources, allowing your fleet to thrive and grow in the vast expanse of space. 


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35809242/4f60fe1f3e0074214a9d341265de5f35e453a5c1.png[/img]
Now for something new! Streamlining your fleet’s capabilities is easier than ever with the Merge Command. By aligning the empty sockets of two stations and pressing the merge button, you can combine ships and create a more powerful, unified station. This simple yet efficient feature helps you optimize your operations, making space management smoother and your fleet stronger.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35809242/6750973f135b3ef5a9db95a8fbbb2805ac971ae9.png[/img]
Once merged, these stations function as a single, unified entity to ensure your space station grows stronger and more capable with each expansion.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35809242/58204edcd437849b171d84db33b276e1f2aab109.png[/img]
The node in this screenshot serves as the foundational structure for creating a larger [b]station hub[/b] in Starminer. With its modular design, it provides the core support necessary for expanding your space station. As you build upon this central hub, you can develop a fully operational, interconnected network capable of handling more advanced systems.


[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35809242/05b54f9e8c768d48913327fe3d6b86b2b1227f70.png[/img]
But you don't have to limit yourself if you don't want to! [i][b]Station hub nodes[/b][/i] can also be stacked together to create larger, more advanced structures. By combining multiple hubs, you can expand your operations and enhance the capabilities of your station. This modular system allows for flexible and scalable growth, adapting to the ever-evolving needs of your fleet and resource management in space.


🪐　 ˚　.　　　 🛸　　.　　　　　　 ✦　　　.　　˚　🌒　　　　. ✦ 　  ˚　.　˚　　☄️　　　✦　　　.　 ˚　.　　 🚀　　.　　　˚　.　　　　 ✦　　　.　　　　. ✦ 　      ˚.　.  　 　　🌍　　˚　　✦　　　　*　　 .˚　 　　　


That's all for this week's screenshot highlight in [i][b]Starminer[/b][/i]! 

As always, we hope you enjoyed this look into building and merging stations to enhance your fleet. How will you strategize your station expansions? Will you stack for power or merge for efficiency? Let us know your thoughts in the comments, and stay tuned for more updates as we continue to bring the universe of [i][b]Starminer[/b][/i] to life!

[b][i]Until next time![/i][/b]

[h3]- Starminer Dev Team 🌌[/h3]

notes.title: Starminer Development Progress Update
notes.content:
Hello everyone!

We have some updates to share about Starminer.

[h2]New Release Window[/h2]
First, we have a new release window for our game, and as a result we won’t release in Early Access this year. We’re now aiming to [b]launch in 2025[/b], and will announce the final release date a bit later.

We understand that a delay is not the kind of news any of you wanted to hear, so we want to share a few things that will hopefully soften the blow a bit!

[h2]Development Progress[/h2]
Most importantly, the development of the game is going well! We made a lot of good progress this year, and we hope you saw it in some of the trailers we shared in recent months. To give you a better idea of what we worked on these past 12 months, here is a "before" and "after" shot of early game of Starminer:

[h3]October 2023 build:[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35809242/c21e67c19a1ac585a84620200a259663bb01affd.jpg[/img]
[h3]November 2024 build:[/h3]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35809242/f739363878717b4ce74f4385e133ed53156e336e.jpg[/img]

What you can probably see first, is increase in modularity and component variety of space rigs and stations, and an example of what you can easily create in the game now, vs a year ago. Some of these new modules we already covered in Developer Diary 6, and we'll tell you more about the many new nodes we introduced, in the coming days!

You can also see some of the progress we've been making with UI. Starminer is a complex game, and to make it a fun experience, we're working hard to make sure the UI and UX make it easier to learn and master the game.

That aside, there is plenty of work being done on various in-game systems. Here is a list of some of the features and content we added or improved over the past year. Deduce from them however much you want... :)

[h3]Development progress October 2023 - November 2024:[/h3]
[list]
[*] Complete interface and UI rehaul
[*] Docking and merging stations
[*] Asteroid hauling - the ability to grab and transport asteroids
[*] Asteroid bases - build modules and installations on asteroids
[*] Over 15 new modules
[*] 2 new "commander" type ships with their own upgrades
[*] Heating system and radiators, with two different types of heat management, radiation and thermal dumping
[*] Officers - hire different officer types with perks to unlock as they level-up (engineering, combat, construction, logistics, science)
[*] New sandbox mode with various customizable settings: location, enemy difficulty, starting resources and more
[*] New campaign mode and rehauled tutorial
[*] Intro story sequence
[*] NPC dialogue system
[*] 6 new starting classes each with different perks to unlock and level-up
[*] Starmap and starmap travel
[*] 10 new space sectors
[*] 2 new resource types: H20 and eonite
[*] 3 types of missions - story missions, bounties, contracts
[*] Revamped research tree and player progression
[*] Autonomous combat frigates
[*] Improved build system for free building in 3d space (construction points)
[*] Updated graphics&FX, loads of optimizations for much better performance 
[*] Full Nvidia DLSS integration
[/list]

Finally, just as a curiosity, here is a shot from the first ever build of Starminer. We've come a long way!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/35809242/d5f9d5b5cf7b4113ca6b418a262ff0ecf3a54d4e.jpg[/img]
[h2]What's next?[/h2]
Together with our publisher, we’re committed to give you the best, hardcore space mining simulation we can, and that’s the main reason why we want to work on Starminer a bit longer.

That said, we know that you want to see more! 

First, we can promise more [b]Developer Diaries and videos[/b] before the release. Next Dev Diary will land this month, and will dive more into the subject of [b]nodes[/b]! There is plenty left to talk about how you can build your stations and ships!

Before the end of the year, we also want to invite you all to join us for a special [b]end-of-year stream[/b]. We’ll play the game, and answer your questions! More details on that will come soon!

For now, we wanted to thank you for your patience! Your support matters a lot and we can’t wait to get Starminer in your hands #whenitsready!

notes.title: ILL Space 0.2.6.0 pre-alpha Released
notes.content:
ILL Space 0.2.6 is out!

This release features a number of gameplay updates and performance optimizations. Check them out:

[b]Additions:[/b]
[list]
[*]Authenticate via Steam or link your Steam account with your existing illspace.com account.
[*] Energy Routing: Hulk Nodes now act as energy routers, meaning you can switch them off and disconnect station branches to optimize energy routing.
[*]Overlays: they provide you with better overview of your economy. Use keys "1" and "2" to activate resource and energy overlays which provide you with additional info.
[*]Time Dilation: Slow down time in critical moments to make better decisions in the heat of battle. Press "P" to activate.
[*]Sentry Mode: Hulk Nodes with weapons attached can now rotate to act as sentries.
[*]Selection Tool: Select (Shift + click, Shift + double click), Delete (Shift + D).
[*]Template Stacking: You can now place build orders on objects which are still under construction.
[/list]
[b]Fixes and Optimizations:[/b]
[list]
[*]GUI performance optimized.
[*]RTX raytracing optimized.
[*]Energy routing optimized (You can now build much larger stations with little performance impact).
[*]Asteroid camera clipping fixed.
[*]Updated upgrade system.
[/list]

This is most likely the last release before the 0.3 version, which will bring you a host of substantial and exciting updates including dynamic single player campaign, new environments, nodes, weapons and enemies! Follow us on our social networks to stay tuned with our development.

notes.title: ILL Space ALPHA 0.2.4 Released
notes.content:
ILL Space has just been updated!

What's new in this 0.2.4 update?

A lot of under-the-hood fixes for optimization and bug riddance, updated lighting for better performance and several quality-of-life additions to make your experience much smoother.

We have also added an experimental [b]Nvidia RTX[/b] support to this build, along with an option to choose between [b]DirectX 11[/b] or [b]12[/b].  [b]Nvidia Ansel[/b] was also implemented - it let's you take great looking screenshots easily (enable with Alt+F2 in game).

Difficulty and resource requirements were tweaked so the leaderboards will be purged.


A very special thanks to our top 3 players!!!
[olist]
[*] [b]mihalp[/b]
[*] [b]rancid_cat[/b]
[*] [b]OBELIKS[/b]
[/olist]
Congratulations and thank you for your invaluable feedback! 

Thanks also to our alpha-testers who have helped us in this initial round - we have many exciting new features and additions in the works for the next major 0.3 update (which will include new environments, enemies, guns, nodes, game modes and a revamped GUI).

Until then, we hope you will continue to help us shape the universe of ILL Space.

notes.title: ILL Space ALPHA 0.2.3 Released
notes.content:
Fellow commanders,

new version of ILL Space is now available!

This version comes with enabled tutorial mode "Learn the Ropes" and other important fixes and updates.


[h1][b]ILL Space - version ALPHA 0.2.3 - Release notes[/b][/h1]

[b]FEATURES & UPDATES[/b]
[list]
[*] Highscore and Account reset.
[*] Highscore not time dependent anymore
[*] New tutorial game mode "Learn the Ropes".
[*] Updated research and upgrade system.
[*] Updated Help shortcut list.
[*] Feedback form now contains Category as selectable dropdown option.
[*] Build Mode Widget animation.
[*] New Skyboxes.
[*] Passive and aggressive enemies.
[*] Construction of module can be cancelled by clicking on Queue icon.
[*] Reclaim 70% of metal when selling modules.
[/list]

[*] Display Info window's "Toggle Operation" button after object is built.
[*] Fixed Tokamak's targeting issues and crashes.
[*] Fixed lasers not firing through Shield.
[*] Fix for objects stuck under construction.
[*] Modules with attached structures can't be sold anymore.
[*] Power distribution fix.
[*] Docked Engineer movement fixed.
[*] Enemy movement optimizations.
[*] Rounding values in resource panel.
[*] Info Window is now disabled for objects under construction.
[*] Fixed issue with Resource points when selling Research Lab under construction.
[*] Toggle mining/military synchronization with newly built modules.
